headline: Discord bug incorrectly bans 8,200 accounts since May
summary: Discord's AI-powered moderation tools mistakenly flagged posts, led to erroneous bans
details: A bug in Discord's moderation tools caused accounts to be incorrectly banned. The issue, which started in May, may have impacted around 8,200 accounts.

The problem arose when the AI-powered content moderation tools mistakenly flagged posts, such as square grid images, as child sexual abuse material. This led to erroneous bans, affecting about 200 accounts over the weekend.

Discord's support team acknowledged the issue and stated that they are working on better safeguards to prevent similar incidents in the future. The company uses AI-powered content moderation tools to compare known harmful material against what its members post.

The support team also mentioned that usually, flagged accounts are reviewed by a person from the company's Trust & Safety team before any action is taken against a user. However, a bug caused the accounts to be banned instead of being temporarily paused during the review process.
Discord has since reinstituted the affected accounts.

headline_marked: X app for iOS gets [[built-in video editor]] with overlay captions
headline: X app for iOS gets built-in video editor with overlay captions
summary: The new video editor includes green screen feature and multilingual captions
details: The X app for iOS now features a built-in video editor and recorder tool. This new tool allows users to add overlay captions in multiple languages with a customized look, as well as a green screen feature.
The video editor is part of X's efforts to encourage users to post more original videos on the app. The platform is trying to compete with video-centric platforms like TikTok.

X's head of product, Nikita Bier, noted that the editor and recorder tool includes options to add custom backgrounds using posts or photos from the camera roll. The company plans to release more updates to the video editor in the coming weeks.
The video editor follows other updates aimed at increasing original video content on the platform, including a video reaction function and $1 million in payouts for live video streamers.
